A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HIPE research, with matching authors, methods, and experiments. The text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison. The removed NeurIPS checklist is identifiable document content, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original active-learning and Bayesian-optimization experiments, including predictive accuracy, optimization performance, runtime measurements, and appendix batch-size analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Figures 2–10 and the runtime table, including the supplementary analyses in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The HIPE objective, hyperparameter-information weighting, fully Bayesian GP model, and parallel Monte Carlo optimization procedure remain unchanged. The revised EPIG background does not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic functions, including the extended Hartmann variants and Ishigami, the same LCBench tasks, and the same 20D/40D SVM problems. The appendix evaluation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within corresponding experiments: BALD, NIPV, Sobol, and Random for active learning; NIPV, LHS-Beta, Sobol, and Random for BO; and NIPV and Random in the runtime comparison.

E3.justification: Batch sizes, evaluation budgets, metrics, noise settings, GP priors, acquisition optimization settings, and data preparation remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same SVM sample and validation split and Monte Carlo sample counts. The new identification of Hartmann 6D for the runtime experiment is additional documentation.

E4.justification: The initialization-size sweep, BO and active-learning batch-size comparisons, and SVM lengthscale analysis are retained. The runtime analysis moves from v1 Section 5.4 to v2 Appendix C.1 with the same evidence; it is not a new supplementary experiment.

E5.justification: The reported seed counts, mean/one-standard-error convention, plotted error bars, and runtime uncertainty values are retained. Figure 2 shortens '100 seeds per benchmark' to '100 seeds,' without reporting a different replication count or uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: All plotted results and numerical table entries are unchanged. The limited change is qualitative: Section 5.3 drops v1's explicit claim that HIPE is top-performing 'on all benchmarks' for the q=8, B=5 LCBench experiment, retaining a less specific top-performing summary.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces v1's incomplete negative-entropy EPIG expression with an explicit predictive mutual-information definition and nested entropy expectation in v2 Equations 4–5. It also derives the Gaussian-likelihood GP simplification in Equation 6. Proposition 1 and its Appendix B proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and discussion retain the same central claims: HIPE balances predictive uncertainty reduction and hyperparameter learning, admits a practical GP implementation, and benefits few-shot, large-batch optimization.

C2.justification: The explanations of hyperparameter identification, calibration versus RMSE tradeoffs, boundary-related inference difficulties, and computational costs remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the GP-specific implementation limitation and the same proposed extensions.

D1.justification: v1 provides the experiment repository and promises future BoTorch availability. v2 retains that repository and reports an available tested BoTorch implementation, adding specific implementation and demonstration-notebook pointers in Appendix A. Section 5.2 also identifies Hartmann 6D as the runtime benchmark. These are documentation changes; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v2 removes Chen and Zhou (2014) from the NIPV attribution and bibliography, retaining Seo et al. (2000). The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged; other reference edits mainly shorten bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: Section 2.3 gains separate NIPV, EPIG, and GP-specific explanations; runtime analysis moves to Appendix C; the licenses and compute subsections swap order; and the NeurIPS checklist is removed. Most scientific prose and the overall research narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The runtime table moves from the main text to Appendix C.1 and becomes Table 2; the noise table becomes Table 1. Figures reflow across pages, with Figures 9 and 10 sharing the final page in v2, and Figure 2's caption is shortened. Plot contents and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical clarity by replacing the incomplete EPIG definition with explicit mutual-information and conditional-entropy formulations and explaining the GP simplification. Specific BoTorch implementation and notebook pointers improve reproducibility documentation. The experimental evidence and substantive limitations are retained, so these are useful but limited gains in clarity and usability.
